info.title: IT Ticketing System API
info.description:
REST API for a role-based IT service desk. Sign in with `POST /auth/login` (demo accounts are listed by `GET /auth/demo-users`), then use **Authorize** to send the returned access token (valid 15 minutes) as a bearer token.

Every response carries an `x-request-id` header; error bodies repeat it as `requestId`, so a reported problem can be matched to a server log line. Send your own `x-request-id` to trace a specific request.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Sign-in with hashed passwords, 15-minute access tokens and rotating refresh cookies.

tags.name: Tickets
tags.description: Ticket lifecycle. Requesters only see and change their own tickets; technicians work the whole queue; only admins delete.

tags.name: Administration
tags.description: Admin-only: who has which role, and the security audit log.

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description: Scheduled work, called by a scheduler with the CRON_SECRET bearer token. Safe to call at any time and as often as you like.

get.description: The process is running. Does not touch the database.
The service can reach its database and is able to serve traffic.

post.description: Checks the email and password (stored as argon2id hashes) and returns a **15-minute access token** to send as a bearer token, plus the user. It also sets the `rt` refresh cookie (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` over https, scoped to `/api/auth`); the browser holds that cookie and the page never sees it. Use `POST /auth/refresh` to get a new access token when it expires. Failed attempts are rate limited per client address; successful sign-ins are not counted.

200.description: Signed in. The refresh cookie is set on this response.

get.description: The seeded accounts and their public demo passwords, so reviewers can try each role. Demo data only.
Filtered, sorted and paginated. Requesters only ever receive their own tickets. Sorting by `priority` ranks by severity (urgent first when descending), not alphabetically.

post.description: Assigns the next ticket number (`TKT-0001`, ...) and an SLA due date from the priority. When a requester creates a ticket, the requester identity, `open` status and `Unassigned` owner are forced by the server.

get.description: Takes the same filters as the list, ignores paging, and returns every matching row. The CSV is streamed from a database cursor in chunks, so a large export does not grow the server's memory. Cells that begin with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are prefixed with an apostrophe so spreadsheets do not run them as formulas.
Counts by status and priority, plus SLA risk, scoped to what the caller may see.
A requester asking for someone else's ticket receives 404, so ticket ids cannot be probed.

patch.description: Every change to status, priority or assignee is recorded in the ticket's activity history. Status moves follow the workflow: `open` to `assigned`, `in-progress` or `closed`; `assigned` to `in-progress` or `open`; `in-progress` to `resolved` or `assigned`; `resolved` to `closed` or `in-progress`; `closed` to `in-progress`, admins only. Any other move is a `409`, and reopening a closed ticket as a non-admin is a `403`. Moving to `resolved` or `closed` stamps `resolvedAt`; reopening clears it and logs `ticket_reopened`. Updates are atomic and versioned: send `If-Match` to avoid overwriting a change you have not seen. Changing priority recalculates the SLA due date unless `dueAt` is sent. Requesters may only change `title`, `description`, `priority` and `category` on their own tickets.

ETag.description: The new ticket version, quoted. Send it as `If-Match` on the next edit.

post.description: Trades the `rt` refresh cookie for a new access token and a new cookie. Refresh tokens are single use: the old one stops working. If a token that was already used is presented again, someone holds a copy, so the whole session is ended (and recorded in the audit log). A role change made since sign-in takes effect here. A request naming a different `Origin` is refused.

200.description: A new access token, and a new refresh cookie.

post.description: Ends the session the `rt` cookie belongs to and clears the cookie. Harmless without a session.

get.description: Admins only. Never includes password hashes.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id (24 hex characters), as returned by `GET /users`.

patch.description: Admins only. There must always be at least one admin, so demoting the last one is a `409` (`LAST_ADMIN`); this holds even when two admins demote each other at the same moment. The change ends the user's sessions, so it applies at their next refresh, and is recorded in the audit log. An access token already issued keeps its old role until it expires (at most 15 minutes).

get.description: Admins only, read-only, newest first. Records sign-ins (successes and failures), sign-outs, detected refresh-token reuse, role changes, ticket deletions and permission denials, with who, from where (address and user agent) and the request id.
Oldest first. A requester receives only public comments; internal notes are never sent to them.

200.description: The comments the caller may read.

post.summary: Add a comment or internal note
post.description: Visibility defaults to public. Only staff may post an internal note; a requester who tries receives 403. Adding a comment does not change the ticket's version.

get.summary: Trends over the last N days
get.description: Tickets opened and resolved per day, mean time to resolve and SLA compliance, for the tickets the caller may see. A day ends at midnight in the requested time zone.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: An IANA time zone name such as America/Toronto. Defaults to UTC.

post.description: Marks unresolved tickets that have passed their deadline (raising the priority one step, without moving the deadline) or are within 24 hours of it. Each step is recorded once on the ticket, so running it again changes nothing.

503.description: `JOBS_NOT_CONFIGURED`: CRON_SECRET is missing or shorter than 32 characters, so the jobs are off.

post.description: Sends events that are due to the configured webhook, retrying failures with exponential backoff. Does nothing when no webhook is configured.

503.description: `JOBS_NOT_CONFIGURED`: CRON_SECRET is missing or shorter than 32 characters, so the jobs are off.

get.description: Events waiting to be sent to the webhook, newest first. Filter by `status=dead` to see what gave up.

post.description: Puts a dead event back in the queue with a fresh set of attempts. Recorded in the audit log.

get.description: Request rate, latency by route template, tickets created, outbox backlog and process metrics, in the Prometheus text format. The endpoint does not exist (404) unless `METRICS_TOKEN` is set on the server. The numbers are per instance, so they are meaningful for a container deployment, not for serverless.

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus text exposition format.

404.description: `METRICS_TOKEN` is not set (or is shorter than 32 characters), so the endpoint is off.

cronAuth.description: The `CRON_SECRET` shared with the scheduler. Not a user token.

metricsAuth.description: The `METRICS_TOKEN` shared with the Prometheus scraper. Not a user token.

TicketId.name: id
TicketId.description: The ticket's MongoDB id (24 hex characters), not its `TKT-` number.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The ticket version the caller last saw (`__v`), as `"3"`, `W/"3"` or `3`. If the ticket has changed since, the update is refused with 409 and nothing is written. Without it the update is applied to the latest version.

schema.description: Defaults to `createdAt`, or to relevance (best match first) when `search` is used and no sort is asked for.

SlaFilter.name: sla
SlaFilter.description: Unresolved tickets that are overdue (`breached`) or due within 24 hours (`due-soon`). Combines with `status`; a resolved or closed status matches nothing.

Search.name: search
Search.description: Full-text search across ticket number, title, description, requester, assignee and category. It matches whole words and their other forms (`connecting` finds `connect`), ignoring case, not fragments of a word. Input of the form `TKT-0012` (or its start) matches ticket numbers by prefix instead. Treated as plain words: search operators such as a leading `-` or quotes have no special meaning.

Forbidden.description: Signed in, but not permitted to do this.

NotFound.description: No such ticket, or one the caller may not see.

Conflict.description: The change conflicts with the ticket's current state: a status move the workflow does not allow, or an `If-Match` version that is no longer current.

TooManyRequests.description: Too many failed sign-in attempts from this address.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The database is not configured or not reachable.

commit.description: Git commit the running build came from.

authConfigured.description: False when AUTH_SECRET is missing or shorter than 32 characters. In production, sign-in and authenticated routes then return 503.

code.description: Stable identifier clients should branch on.

requestId.description: Matches the `x-request-id` response header and the server log line.

exp.description: Token expiry, seconds since the epoch.

actorRole.description: `system` for a change made by an automated job (such as SLA escalation) rather than a person.

actorEmail.description: Absent for a change made by an automated job.

internal.description: True for an entry about an internal note. Only staff receive these entries.

__v.description: Ticket version, incremented on every update. Send it back as `If-Match` to refuse the edit if the ticket changed in the meantime.

dueAt.description: SLA deadline, derived from priority unless set explicitly.

slaAtRiskAt.description: When the SLA job first saw the ticket within 24 hours of its deadline. Set once.

slaBreachedAt.description: When the SLA job first saw the deadline pass, and raised the priority one step. Set once.

tickets.description: Same rows as `data`, kept for older clients.

TicketPatch.description: Send only the fields to change. Unknown fields are ignored; a body with none is rejected.

actor.description: Who did it. Absent for a failed sign-in, where nobody is authenticated.

CommentVisibility.description: Who may read a comment. Internal notes are for staff; a requester never receives one.

series.description: One entry per calendar day, oldest first. Days with nothing in them are zeros.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD in the requested time zone.

resolved.description: Tickets resolved or closed that day.

meanHours.description: Mean time from creation to resolution, in hours to one decimal place. Null when nothing was resolved.

met.description: Resolved on or before the SLA deadline.

compliancePercent.description: Share of resolved tickets that met their deadline, to one decimal place. Null when nothing was resolved.

OutboxStatus.description: pending: waiting to be sent or retried. sending: claimed by a worker. delivered: the webhook accepted it. dead: gave up after the sixth attempt; an admin can retry it.

payload.description: What is sent to the webhook. Never contains comment text or ticket descriptions.

lastError.description: Why the last attempt failed. The webhook address is never included.

breached.description: Tickets that had just passed their deadline; each was raised one priority step (unless already urgent).

atRisk.description: Tickets newly within 24 hours of their deadline.

more.description: True when the run stopped at its limit with more still to do; the next run continues.

configured.description: False when no webhook is configured; nothing else happens in that case.

retried.description: Sent unsuccessfully and put back for another try.

dead.description: Sent unsuccessfully for the last time.
